title: mentha longifolia subsp. lavandulacea
intro: Mentha longifolia subsp. lavandulacea, commonly known as Hoary Bergamot or Wild Bergamot, is a subspecies of the peppermint plant. It has been traditionally used for its numerous health benefits, including reducing inflammation, relieving digestive issues, and improving respiratory problems. The plant's therapeutic actions include its antiseptic, anti-inflammatory, and antispasmodic properties, which contribute to its use in treating various health conditions. The bioactive constituents of Hoary Bergamot include menthone, limonene, and beta-pinene, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
